hook.text: Trucks carry 72% of all freight by value in the United States. The highway is the supply chain's backbone.

buildup.text: Road freight offers door-to-door delivery, flexible scheduling, and coverage to places rail and ships can't reach.

discovery.text: Full truckload (FTL) fills one trailer. Less-than-truckload (LTL) combines shipments from multiple shippers.

twist.text: Trucks are the most expensive mode per ton-mile. Fuel, drivers, and tolls add up fast.

climax.text: Despite the cost, speed and flexibility make road freight irreplaceable for most supply chains.

punchline.text: If it's on a shelf, a truck probably put it there.

quiz.question: What share of US freight by value moves by truck?
